question: Who wrote the book Friends Not Masters?
reason: Friends Not Masters (1967, Oxford University Press) is the political autobiography of President Muhammad Ayub Khan.

question: Adolf Hitler was the dictator of which country during the Second World War?
reason: Hitler led the Nazi Party and ruled Germany as Chancellor and Fuhrer from 1933 until his death in 1945. He started the war by invading Poland in 1939.

question: According to the 1956 Constitution, the President of Pakistan was elected by:
answer: An electoral college of members of the National and Provincial Assemblies
reason: The 1956 Constitution had a President elected for 5 years by members of the National and Provincial Assemblies; Basic Democrats were used in the 1962 Constitution.

question: Who was the ruler of Sindh when Muhammad bin Qasim conquered it in 712 AD?
reason: Raja Dahir of the Chach dynasty was defeated and killed at the Battle of Aror (Rohri) by Muhammad bin Qasim.

question: Who is the current Chief of the Naval Staff of Pakistan?
reason: Admiral Naveed Ashraf has been Chief of the Naval Staff since 7 October 2023 and was still serving in 2026.

question: Who introduced the Basic Democracies System in Pakistan in 1959?
reason: President Ayub Khan introduced the Basic Democracies Order in October 1959. Union councils elected Basic Democrats who later formed an electoral college.

question: Which tree is the national tree of Pakistan?
reason: The deodar (Cedrus deodara), a cedar of the northern mountains, is the national tree of Pakistan.

question: Where is the headquarters of Amnesty International located?
reason: Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 and its International Secretariat is based in London.

question: In which year did the Khilafat Movement begin?
reason: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 under the Ali brothers and others to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.

question: How many nuclear tests did Pakistan conduct on 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I)?
reason: Chagai-I was five simultaneous underground tests at the Ras Koh Hills, Balochistan, on 28 May 1998. A further test (Chagai-II) followed on 30 May.

question: When the actual words of the speaker are reported exactly as spoken, inside quotation marks, it is called:
reason: In direct speech (direct narration) the exact words are quoted. In indirect speech they are reported in the reporter's own words.

question: In which year did the Hijrat (migration) of the Prophet ﷺ from Makkah to Madinah take place?
reason: The Prophet ﷺ migrated from Makkah to Madinah in 622 AD, which is year 1 of the Islamic Hijri calendar.

question: In which year was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
reason: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969 after Ayub Khan resigned.

question: On which date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
reason: The UN General Assembly admitted Pakistan (with Yemen) on 30 September 1947 by resolution 108 (II).

question: Which agreement ended the 1965 Pakistan-India war?
reason: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri, with Soviet Premier Kosygin mediating.

question: On which date did the United States declare its independence?
reason: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776, celebrated as Independence Day in the USA.

question: In which year was the War of Independence (against the British East India Company) fought?
reason: The War of Independence of 1857 was the major uprising against British rule in the subcontinent, ending Mughal rule.

question: Who was called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity by Sarojini Naidu?
reason: Sarojini Naidu gave Jinnah this title for his role in the 1916 Lucknow Pact between Congress and the Muslim League.

question: Who is the President of China (as of October 2026)?
reason: Xi Jinping is President of the People's Republic of China (and General Secretary of the Communist Party). Li Qiang is the Premier.

question: What is the capital of Bhutan?
reason: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan; Punakha was the old capital until 1955.

question: Ahmad is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will the sister be when Ahmad is 10 years old?
reason: Sister is 3 x 5 = 15 now. Ahmad needs 5 more years to reach 10, so the sister will be 15 + 5 = 20.

question: In which year did the Al-Khalid main battle tank enter service with the Pakistan Army?
reason: Al-Khalid (MBT-2000) was developed jointly by Pakistan and China, and the first batch entered Pakistan Army service in 2001. The improved Al-Khalid-I was inducted in 2020.

question: What was the relation of Abu Talib with Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
reason: Abu Talib was a son of Abd al-Muttalib and so the paternal uncle of the Prophet; he took care of him after the death of his grandfather.

question: Who wrote the lyrics of the National Anthem (Qaumi Tarana) of Pakistan?
reason: The lyrics were written by Abu al-Asar Hafeez Jalandhari, while the music was composed by Ahmad Ghulam Ali Chagla. It was officially adopted in 1954.

question: What is the capital of Iran?
reason: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran.

question: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the partition in August 1947?
reason: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India (1947) and oversaw the partition. Lord Wavell was his predecessor.

question: Zabihullah (the one offered for sacrifice) is the title of which Prophet?
reason: Hazrat Ismail (A.S.) is known as Zabihullah, the son Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.) was ready to sacrifice at Allah's command.

question: In which year was the One Unit scheme implemented in Pakistan?
reason: The One Unit scheme merged the western provinces into West Pakistan in 1955 (Act passed 30 September 1955, in force 14 October 1955) and was ended in 1970.

question: In 2020, Kashmir Highway in Islamabad was renamed as:
reason: In August 2020 Kashmir Highway was renamed Srinagar Highway to show solidarity with Kashmiris on the first Youm-e-Istehsal.

question: In which city is the Pakistan Navy Headquarters (Naval Headquarters) located?
reason: Naval Headquarters was shifted from Karachi to Islamabad in 1975 and is in Sector E-9, Islamabad.

question: Cow is to milk as dog is to ?
reason: A cow gives milk and a dog gives a bark, the thing it produces.

question: Who started the Faraizi movement in Bengal?
reason: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi movement in 1818 to make Bengali Muslims follow the obligatory duties (faraiz) of Islam. His son Dudu Miyan later led it.

question: Which is the national bird of Pakistan?
reason: The chukar partridge (chakor) is the national bird of Pakistan.

question: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, ?
reason: Positions are 1, 3, 6, 10: gaps of 2, 3, 4. Next is 10, which is J.

question: According to a hadith in Sahih Muslim, which voluntary (nafl) prayer is the best after the obligatory prayers?
reason: The Prophet (PBUH) said the best prayer after the obligatory prayers is the night prayer, which is Tahajjud (Sahih Muslim).

question: Which continent is the coldest on Earth?
reason: Antarctica has the lowest recorded temperature on Earth, minus 89.2 degrees C at Vostok Station on 21 July 1983.

question: How many sons did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) have?
reason: The Prophet (SAW) had three sons: Qasim, Abdullah (also called Tayyib and Tahir) and Ibrahim. All of them died in childhood.

question: Who led the Salt March (Dandi March) of 1930?
reason: Gandhi led 78 followers about 387 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, starting on 12 March 1930.

question: In which year did the Swadeshi Movement begin?
reason: The partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905 and the boycott of British goods was resolved on 7 August 1905.

question: In which year was the Home Rule Movement launched in India?
reason: Both Home Rule Leagues, of Tilak and of Annie Besant, were founded in 1916.

question: Who led the anti-apartheid struggle in South Africa?
reason: Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison for resisting apartheid and became South Africa's first democratically elected president in 1994.
